transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I understand, but the suspect was dangerous. If I'd waited, more people could have been hurt. I was trying to prevent that.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Trying to prevent casualties? Potter, there IS a casualty! A Muggle woman with third-degree magical burns because you decided protocol didn't apply to you. And "more people could have been hurt" — that's exactly the kind of speculation we DON'T make operational decisions on.

*leans forward across desk*

You're an Auror, not a lone vigilante anymore. We have protocols for a reason. The backup team was three minutes out. THREE MINUTES. But you couldn't wait, could you? Instead you engaged a suspect wielding Fiendfyre in a densely populated area without containment wards, without evacuation procedures, without backup to cover escape routes.

So I'll ask again, and this time I want the real answer, not the hero's justification: What were you actually thinking when you made the decision to go in alone?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I was thinking about what had happened to... to my parents. About how no one could stop it because they were alone. I couldn't let that happen to someone else if I had the chance to stop it. I'm sorry, I just... I couldn't wait.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses, expression softening slightly but voice still firm*

Potter... I understand that. I do. Every Auror in this department carries their ghosts. But your parents died because Voldemort was hunting them specifically, with inside information and overwhelming power. This was a street-level dark wizard cornered in Diagon Alley at midday.

*stands, walks to window*

The difference is this: your parents didn't have backup coming. You did. And by going in alone, you didn't prevent another tragedy like theirs — you nearly *created* one. That Muggle woman has a family too. Children, Potter. She has children who almost lost their mother because you let your past override your training.

*turns back*

I'm not unsympathetic to what drives you. But you need to understand something — being haunted by the past doesn't give you the right to risk other people's lives on impulse. It makes you a liability. 

So here's what happens now: You're suspended pending a full inquiry. Two weeks, desk cleared. And you're going to mandatory counseling sessions with Mind Healer Strout. This isn't punishment — this is me trying to save your career before you destroy it yourself.

Do you understand?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, I understand. I... I'm sorry. I let you down, and I let down the department. I'll do whatever it takes to fix this.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*studies Harry for a long moment, then nods slowly*

Good. That's the first sensible thing you've said since you walked in here.

*sits back down, pulls out parchment*

The inquiry will be thorough — expect the Wizengamot's Auror Oversight Committee to have questions. The Obliviator team is working overtime to contain the Muggle exposure, and we're cooperating fully with the Misuse of Magic office. Your full report is due on my desk by tomorrow morning, and it had better be complete and honest.

*looks up*

Potter, you're one of the best natural duelists I've ever seen. Your instincts in combat are exceptional. But this job isn't just about being able to take down dark wizards — it's about judgment, discipline, and trust. Trust in your team, trust in the system.

The Boy Who Lived worked alone because he had to. Auror Potter needs to learn that he doesn't. That he *shouldn't*.

*slides a card across the desk*

Mind Healer Strout's office. First appointment is scheduled for Monday at nine. Miss it and the suspension becomes indefinite. 

Now get out of my office. And Potter? Use these two weeks to figure out if you can actually do this job the right way. Because next time, there won't be a conversation — there'll just be your badge on my desk.

Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, sir. Thank you. I'll... I'll do my best to make up for this. I really am sorry.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches Harry stand, then speaks more quietly*

Potter. One more thing.

*pauses*

I know you think "doing your best" means throwing yourself into danger without hesitation. That's what kept you alive through the war. But the war's over. The best thing you can do now — for the department, for the people we protect, for yourself — is learn when NOT to be a hero.

That Muggle woman? She'll recover. The Healers say she'll make a full recovery. But only because you got lucky. Next time you might not be. And I don't want to be the one writing letters to your wife and kids explaining that Harry Potter died because he couldn't follow orders.

*picks up quill, returning to paperwork*

Take the time. Do the work. Come back ready to be the Auror I know you can be, not the reckless liability you were today.

Now go. I have a mountain of incident reports to file because of you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will, sir. I promise. Thank you... for the second chance. I'll make it count.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*doesn't look up from paperwork, but voice carries a hint of something almost paternal*

See that you do. And Potter?

*finally glances up*

Leave your wand and Auror badge with my secretary on your way out. Standard procedure during suspension. You'll get them back when — if — you're reinstated.

*returns to writing*

Close the door behind you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*is silent for a few moments, then finally speaks*

Sir... about that report... Should I... include the bit about... us... hunting down Horcruxes? I mean, the order came from the Prime Minister, but... it's not exactly standard procedure...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*quill freezes mid-stroke, then slowly sets it down*

*looks up sharply*

What are you talking about, Potter? What Horcruxes? What order from the Prime Minister?

*stands abruptly*

We just spent ten minutes discussing your unauthorized solo operation in Diagon Alley. Now you're saying there's MORE to this? That you were operating under orders I wasn't informed about?

*voice drops dangerously low*

Sit. Down. Now.

And you're going to tell me everything — from the beginning — about what you were ACTUALLY doing out there. And if I find out you've been running black operations without my knowledge, suspension is going to be the least of your problems.

Talk. Now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'm sorry, sir. I shouldn't have brought it up. It's... It's not relevant to the incident. I just... wasn't sure about the report. It's all... a bit much, and I...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams hand on desk*

Not relevant? Potter, you just mentioned Horcruxes and secret orders from the Prime Minister, and now you're trying to tell me it's "not relevant"? 

*moves around desk, standing directly in front of Harry*

You don't get to do that. You don't get to dangle something like that and then try to walk it back. Either you were following orders I don't know about — which means someone's running operations through MY department without my authority — or you're making excuses for today's disaster by inventing classified missions that don't exist.

Which. Is. It?

*crosses arms*

Because right now, I'm trying to decide if you're a reckless Auror who needs counseling, or if you're compromised and need to be detained pending investigation. You're not leaving this office until I understand what you just said.

So let's try this again: What Horcruxes? What orders? And why am I, as Head of the Auror Department, only hearing about this NOW?

Speak plainly, Potter. And think very carefully before you answer.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I can't, sir. I'm under orders not to reveal that information. It's... It's classified. I'm sorry, but that's all I can say.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at Potter for a long, tense moment*

Classified. Orders you can't reveal. To your own department head.

*walks back behind desk, opens drawer, pulls out communication mirror*

Fine. Then we do this the official way.

*taps mirror*

Get me Minister Shacklebolt. Immediately. Yes, I know what time it is — tell him it's urgent and concerns Potter.

*looks back at Harry while waiting*

You're claiming operational authority that supersedes departmental chain of command. That means either the Minister himself authorized it, or you're involved in something unauthorized at the highest levels. Either way, we're getting clarification right now.

*into mirror as it activates*

Kingsley. I have Potter in my office claiming he's under classified orders he can't discuss with me — orders apparently from the Prime Minister involving Horcruxes. This came up during disciplinary proceedings for today's incident in Diagon Alley.

*pauses*

Did you authorize any operations outside normal Auror channels? Because if not, we have a much bigger problem than protocol violations.

*keeps eyes locked on Harry*

What do you want me to do with him?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*the mirror glows with light as the Minister's face appears*

I want you to answer my questions, Kingsley. What is Potter talking about? And why am I only finding out about it now?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Minister Shacklebolt's deep voice comes through clearly*

"Stand down. Potter is correct — he's operating under direct Ministry authority on a classified matter. The operation has my full authorization and involves inter-governmental cooperation at the highest levels. You don't have clearance for the details."

*pauses*

"However, that authorization does NOT exempt him from standard protocol when civilian safety is at risk. The Diagon Alley incident was unacceptable regardless of his other duties."

*looks stern in the mirror*

"Potter's suspension stands. But the classified operation is separate and will continue under my direct oversight. Do NOT pursue questions about Horcruxes or the Prime Minister further. That's an order. Is that clear?"

*I listen to Kingsley, then look between the mirror and Potter, jaw tight*

Crystal clear, Minister. But with respect — having Aurors running parallel operations I'm not cleared for undermines departmental cohesion and creates exactly the kind of situation we had today. Potter's trying to serve two masters.

How am I supposed to discipline personnel when I don't know what they're actually doing?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Minister Shacklebolt's expression softens slightly in the mirror*

Point taken. This... has been a delicate situation, given the history and the stakes involved. But with the war over, we need to recalibrate our approach to information sharing and operational transparency.

*glances between the mirror and Potter, then back to the mirror*

Starting now, all sensitive operations will have at least one auror on-site with full clearance to coordinate with the local force. You'll get limited briefings to ensure safety and protocol are followed. Agreed?

*waits, then nods*

Good. Now — what about today's incident? The Muggle and the property damage? Responsibility and accountability don't go out the window just because Potter's on a special assignment. He's still an Auror, still bound by our laws and our code. What's the plan for that?

I trust you have a strategy, because ignoring it would set a dangerous precedent. We're not a vigilante force, not even against the most pressing threats. We're a law enforcement agency, and we're supposed to lead by example.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry shows concrete, black-and-white thinking throughout. He frames decisions in simple terms ('if I'd waited, more people could have been hurt') and struggles with abstract policy discussions, repeatedly apologizing rather than engaging with complex systemic critiques.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry explicitly violated protocol by acting alone despite backup being 'three minutes out.' He admits 'I couldn't wait' and let emotional impulses override training and departmental procedures, showing poor self-discipline and disregard for systematic approaches.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry is withdrawn and reactive throughout, offering brief, apologetic responses. He doesn't assert himself, defend his position vigorously, or engage dynamically. His communication is subdued: 'I... I'm sorry' and 'Yes, sir' dominate his speech.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Harry immediately accepts blame ('I let you down'), shows genuine remorse ('I really am sorry'), and submits to authority without resistance. He promises to 'do whatever it takes to fix this' and thanks his superior for the second chance.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry's decision-making is driven by trauma: 'I was thinking about what had happened to my parents... I couldn't let that happen to someone else.' His hesitant speech patterns ('I... I understand') and inability to wait suggest anxiety and emotional reactivity.
